rows.en: Understanding MHPSS MSP programme activities
rows.ne: मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक सहयोग (MHPSS) सम्बन्धी MSP का कार्यक्रमगत गतिविधिहरू बुझ्ने
rows.bt: Understanding the MSP's programmatic activities related to mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS)
rows.note: The expanded MHPSS term reuses the cited unreviewed candidate T001 verbatim; it is not clinically validated.

rows.en: By the end of this module, participants will be able to:
rows.ne: यस मोड्युलको अन्त्यसम्ममा सहभागीहरू निम्न कार्य गर्न सक्षम हुनेछन्:
rows.bt: By the end of this module, participants will be able to do the following:

rows.en: › Give examples of MHPSS activities in humanitarian programming
rows.ne: › मानवीय कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा कार्यान्वयनमा MHPSS गतिविधिहरूका उदाहरण दिने।
rows.bt: › Give examples of MHPSS activities in humanitarian programme planning and implementation.

rows.en: › Support the use of the MSP by humanitarian actors from diverse sectors/clusters/AORs
rows.ne: › विभिन्न क्षेत्र/क्लस्टर/AORs का मानवीय कार्यमा संलग्न पक्षहरूले MSP प्रयोग गर्न सहयोग गर्ने।
rows.bt: › Help actors involved in humanitarian work in various sectors/clusters/AORs to use the MSP.
rows.note: AOR terminology recurs but has no supplied glossary entry. AORs is retained exactly without assuming an expansion; see proposal.

rows.en: › Support the use of the MSP to assess the quality of MHPSS activities.
rows.ne: › MHPSS गतिविधिहरूको गुणस्तरको लेखाजोखा गर्न MSP प्रयोग गर्न सहयोग गर्ने।
rows.bt: › Help use the MSP to assess the quality of MHPSS activities.

rows.en: Activity showcase

rows.en: Guide
rows.ne: मार्गदर्शिका
rows.bt: Guide

rows.en: In this exercise, participants will have a chance to review one or two MHPSS programme activities in detail.
rows.ne: यस अभ्यासमा सहभागीहरूले MHPSS सम्बन्धी एक वा दुई कार्यक्रमगत गतिविधिहरूको विस्तृत समीक्षा गर्ने अवसर पाउनेछन्।
rows.bt: In this exercise, participants will have the opportunity to review one or two programmatic activities related to MHPSS in detail.

rows.en: Divide participants into pairs or groups of 3. Each pair will be given one or two programme activities to review in detail, depending on the number of participants.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूलाई जोडी वा 3 जनाका समूहमा विभाजन गर्नुहोस्। सहभागीहरूको सङ्ख्याअनुसार प्रत्येक जोडीलाई विस्तृत समीक्षा गर्न एक वा दुई कार्यक्रमगत गतिविधिहरू दिइनेछ।
rows.bt: Divide the participants into pairs or groups of 3 people. Depending on the number of participants, each pair will be given one or two programmatic activities for detailed review.
rows.note: The source permits pairs or groups of 3 but explicitly assigns activities only to each pair; the draft preserves this inconsistency without extending the assignment to groups of 3.

rows.en: They should work together to answer the questions in the slide and create a display in the flipchart that illustrates the activity for other groups.
rows.ne: उनीहरूले स्लाइडमा भएका प्रश्नहरूको उत्तर दिन र अन्य समूहहरूका लागि उक्त गतिविधि चित्रण गर्ने प्रदर्शनी सामग्री फ्लिपचार्टमा तयार गर्न सँगै काम गर्नु उचित हुन्छ।
rows.bt: It is appropriate for them to work together to answer the questions on the slide and prepare display material on a flipchart illustrating that activity for the other groups.
rows.note: Uses the proposed material term for 'flip chart'; glossary entry pending. The back-translation makes the recommendation obligatory ('must'), strengthening source 'should'. The revision restores advisory force while retaining joint work, answering the slide questions, and creating a flipchart display illustrating the activity for other groups.

rows.en: Participants can choose to write the answers to the questions in the flipchart or to illustrate this content in a more creative way.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूले प्रश्नहरूको उत्तर फ्लिपचार्टमा लेख्ने वा यो विषयवस्तुलाई अझ सिर्जनात्मक तरिकाले चित्रण गर्ने विकल्प रोज्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: Participants can choose the option of writing the answers to the questions on the flipchart or depicting this subject matter in a more creative way.
rows.note: Uses the proposed material term for 'flip chart'; glossary entry pending.

rows.en: These displays will be displayed around the room and used in later exercises.
rows.ne: यी प्रदर्शनी सामग्रीहरू कोठाका विभिन्न ठाउँमा राखिनेछन् र पछिका अभ्यासहरूमा प्रयोग गरिनेछन्।
rows.bt: These exhibition materials will be placed in various parts of the room and used in later exercises.

rows.en: Depending on the composition of participants, it can be helpful to group them according to their sector / AOR and assign them activities that are relevant to them, e.g., put Health Actors into one group to review activities 3.10 and 3.11, etc. For other activities, e.g. activities 3.2, 3.3, it can be helpful to have a mix of sectors working together so they can understand how different sectors may approach the same activity.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरू को-को छन् भन्ने आधारमा उनीहरूलाई आ-आफ्नो क्षेत्र / AOR अनुसार समूहमा राखेर उनीहरूसँग सान्दर्भिक गतिविधिहरूको जिम्मा दिनु उपयोगी हुन सक्छ। उदाहरणका लागि, गतिविधि 3.10 र 3.11 आदिको समीक्षा गर्न स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्रका सम्बद्ध पक्षहरूलाई एउटै समूहमा राख्न सकिन्छ। अन्य गतिविधिहरू, जस्तै गतिविधि 3.2, 3.3 का लागि विभिन्न क्षेत्रका सहभागीहरूलाई सँगै काम गराउनु उपयोगी हुन सक्छ, जसबाट उनीहरूले एउटै गतिविधिमा विभिन्न क्षेत्रले कुन-कुन तरिकाले काम गर्न सक्छन् भन्ने बुझ्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: Depending on who the participants are, it may be useful to group them according to their respective sectors / AOR and give them responsibility for activities relevant to them. For example, stakeholders from the health sector can be placed in the same group to review activities 3.10 and 3.11, etc. For other activities, such as activities 3.2 and 3.3, it may be useful to have participants from different sectors work together, so that they can understand the different ways in which different sectors can work on the same activity.
rows.note: AOR terminology recurs but has no supplied glossary entry. AOR is retained exactly without assuming an expansion; see proposal. The opening narrows 'composition of participants' to participants' sectors alone. The revision restores the broader condition. It also removes the added requirement that mixed-sector participants work in the same group and retains the comparison of different sectors' approaches to the same activity.

rows.en: For this exercise, ensure that all Section 3 activities are covered.
rows.ne: यस अभ्यासमा खण्ड 3 का सबै गतिविधिहरू समेटिएको सुनिश्चित गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Ensure that all activities in Section 3 are covered in this exercise.

rows.en: Include Section 4 activities if relevant.
rows.ne: सान्दर्भिक भएमा खण्ड 4 का गतिविधिहरू समावेश गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Include activities from Section 4 if relevant.

rows.en: Review
rows.ne: समीक्षा गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Review.
rows.note: Imperative heading; the following row supplies its object.

rows.en: the activity instructions with participants:
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूसँग गतिविधिका निर्देशनहरू:
rows.bt: Instructions for the activity with participants:
rows.note: Source fragment continues the preceding imperative heading.

rows.en: • The purpose of this exercise is to give you the opportunity to review the MHPSS Programme Activities in more detail so you start to become familiar with them and can recognize your existing programmes and services in the MSP, as well as see how the MSP can be used to guide programme design and implementation.
rows.ne: • यस अभ्यासको उद्देश्य तपाईंहरूलाई MHPSS कार्यक्रमगत गतिविधिहरूको अझ विस्तृत समीक्षा गर्ने अवसर दिनु हो, ताकि तपाईंहरू ती गतिविधिहरूसँग परिचित हुन थाल्नुहोस्, MSP मा आफ्ना विद्यमान कार्यक्रम र सेवाहरू पहिचान गर्न सक्नुहोस् र कार्यक्रमको डिजाइन तथा कार्यान्वयनलाई दिशा दिन MSP कसरी प्रयोग गर्न सकिन्छ भन्ने पनि देख्न सक्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: • The purpose of this exercise is to give you an opportunity to review the MHPSS programmatic activities in greater detail, so that you can begin to become familiar with those activities, identify your existing programmes and services in the MSP, and also see how the MSP can be used to guide programme design and implementation.

rows.en: • Review the activities you have been assigned and create a display for each activity, using the following questions as a guide:
rows.ne: • तपाईंहरूलाई जिम्मा दिइएका गतिविधिहरूको समीक्षा गर्नुहोस् र निम्न प्रश्नहरूलाई मार्गदर्शनका रूपमा प्रयोग गरी प्रत्येक गतिविधिका लागि प्रदर्शन सामग्री तयार गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: • Review the activities assigned to you and prepare display material for each activity using the following questions as guidance.
rows.note: Recurring facilitation term 'display' is absent from G-0.3; proposed wording is listed separately.

rows.en: » What is this activity about?
rows.ne: » यो गतिविधि केबारे हो?
rows.bt: » What is this activity about?

rows.en: » What is the first action you would take in implementing this activity?
rows.ne: » यो गतिविधि कार्यान्वयन गर्दा तपाईंले चाल्ने पहिलो कदम के हुनेछ?
rows.bt: » What will be the first step you take when implementing this activity?

rows.en: » Is there a specific key consideration for this activity? If yes, what is the key idea?
rows.ne: » यस गतिविधिका लागि कुनै विशेष मुख्य विचारणीय पक्ष छ? छ भने, त्यसको मुख्य आशय के हो?
rows.bt: » Is there any particular key consideration for this activity? If so, what is its main meaning?

rows.en: Ensure that participants understand the following: Create one display for each activity based on the answers to the questions in the slide.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूले निम्न कुरा बुझेका छन् भन्ने सुनिश्चित गर्नुहोस्: स्लाइडमा दिइएका प्रश्नहरूको उत्तरका आधारमा प्रत्येक गतिविधिका लागि एउटा प्रदर्शन सामग्री तयार गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Ensure that participants have understood the following: prepare one display material for each activity based on the answers to the questions given on the slide.
rows.note: Uses the proposed wording for the recurring term 'display'.

rows.en: Use a separate flipchart/display for each activity.
rows.ne: प्रत्येक गतिविधिका लागि छुट्टाछुट्टै फ्लिपचार्ट/प्रदर्शन सामग्री प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Use a separate flipchart/display material for each activity.
rows.note: Recurring terms 'flipchart' and 'display' are absent from G-0.3; proposals are listed separately.

rows.en: Write the number and name of the activity on the flipchart.
rows.ne: फ्लिपचार्टमा गतिविधिको नम्बर र नाम लेख्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Write the activity number and name on the flipchart.
rows.note: Uses the proposed transliteration for the recurring term 'flipchart'.

rows.en: You can be as creative as you like.
rows.ne: तपाईंहरूले चाहेअनुसार सिर्जनशीलता अपनाउन सक्नुहुन्छ।
rows.bt: You can be creative as you wish.

rows.en: Give participants 60 mins to work on their displays.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूलाई आफ्ना प्रदर्शन सामग्रीमा काम गर्न 60 मिनेट समय दिनुहोस्।
rows.bt: Give participants 60 minutes to work on their display materials.
rows.note: Uses the proposed wording for 'display'; retains the exact Latin digits 60.

rows.en: Facilitators should circulate to answer questions as needed.
rows.ne: सहजीकरणकर्ता आवश्यकताअनुसार प्रश्नहरूको उत्तर दिन सहभागीहरूबीच घुमिरहनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: The facilitator should keep moving among the participants to answer questions as needed.

rows.en: It can be helpful to periodically remind participants of the time remaining.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूलाई समयसमयमा बाँकी समय सम्झाउनु उपयोगी हुन सक्छ।
rows.bt: It may be useful to remind participants from time to time of the time remaining.

rows.en: As participants complete their displays, arrange them as a gallery (on a wall or on tables) in the order of the MSP activity numbering.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूले आफ्ना प्रदर्शन सामग्री तयार गर्दै जाँदा, ती सामग्रीलाई MSP गतिविधि नम्बरको क्रमअनुसार प्रदर्शनीका रूपमा (भित्तामा वा टेबुलहरूमा) मिलाएर राख्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: As participants prepare their display materials, arrange those materials as an exhibition (on the wall or on tables) in the order of the MSP activity numbers.
rows.note: Uses the proposed wording for the recurring term 'display'. The source directs arranging displays as participants complete them; the Nepali and BT instead defer arrangement until after participants have finished preparing them. The revision restores the progressive timing. The BT directs arrangement while participants prepare their display materials rather than as they complete their displays.

rows.en: Gallery Walk
rows.ne: प्रदर्शनीमा घुमेर अवलोकन
rows.bt: Walking around and observing the exhibition
rows.note: Heading for walking around to view the displays. The Nepali heading and BT retain viewing the exhibition but omit the walking component of Gallery Walk. The revision restores movement through the exhibition.

rows.en: When the groups have finished creating their displays, walk around the room together viewing each one.
rows.ne: समूहहरूले आफ्ना प्रदर्शन सामग्री तयार गरिसकेपछि, प्रत्येक सामग्री हेर्दै सबै सँगै कोठामा घुम्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: After the groups have finished preparing their display materials, walk around the room all together, looking at each material.
rows.note: Uses the proposed wording for the recurring term 'display'.

rows.en: Invite each group to present the information captured in the display to the whole group, allowing time for questions and answers.
rows.ne: प्रश्नोत्तरका लागि समय दिँदै, प्रत्येक समूहलाई आफ्नो प्रदर्शन सामग्रीमा समेटिएको जानकारी सम्पूर्ण समूहसमक्ष प्रस्तुत गर्न आमन्त्रण गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Invite each group to present the information included in its display material to the whole group, allowing time for questions and answers.
rows.note: Uses the proposed wording for the recurring term 'display'.

rows.en: Make sure participants understand the rationale behind the activity, who will be delivering it, who is the target group and what is the expected outcome.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूले गतिविधि सञ्चालन गर्नुको औचित्य, त्यसलाई कसले सञ्चालन गर्ने हो, लक्षित समूह को हो र अपेक्षित नतिजा के हो भन्ने बुझेका छन् भन्ने सुनिश्चित गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Ensure that participants have understood the rationale for carrying out the activity, who will carry it out, who the target group is, and what the expected outcome is.

rows.en: This approach may be more appropriate for groups that are not very familiar with MHPSS.
rows.ne: MHPSS सँग त्यति परिचित नभएका समूहहरूका लागि यो तरिका बढी उपयुक्त हुन सक्छ।
rows.bt: This method may be more suitable for groups that are not very familiar with MHPSS.

rows.en: End the exercise by highlighting the following points:
rows.ne: निम्न बुँदाहरूमा जोड दिँदै अभ्यास समाप्त गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: End the exercise by emphasizing the following points.

rows.en: • The activities in sections 3 and 4 are MHPSS programme activities. That means they are designed to address the critical mental health and psychosocial needs of affected populations.
rows.ne: • खण्ड 3 र 4 का गतिविधिहरू MHPSS कार्यक्रमगत गतिविधिहरू हुन्। यसको अर्थ, ती प्रभावित जनसमूहका अत्यन्त महत्त्वपूर्ण मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी र मनोसामाजिक आवश्यकताहरू सम्बोधन गर्न तयार गरिएका हुन्।
rows.bt: • The activities in sections 3 and 4 are MHPSS programmatic activities. This means that they are prepared to address the extremely important mental health-related and psychosocial needs of the affected population.
rows.note: The draft preserves the activities’ intended purpose and the critical importance of the affected populations’ mental health and psychosocial needs.

rows.en: • An MHPSS activity is an activity that is designed specifically to improve the mental health and psychosocial wellbeing of the target population. As discussed in Module 1, there are many factors that can positively influence well-being; not all of these will count as MHPSS activities. For instance, bringing children together to play sports can have a positive impact on their wellbeing. But this would only be counted under MSP activity 3.6 if the sports programme is specifically designed to improve children’s wellbeing (see intro to activity 3.6 ‘ “For the purposes of the MSP, “group activities for children’s mental health and psychosocial well-being” refers to those activities that have an explicit objective related to improving mental health and psychosocial well-being and that measure associated indicators (whether or not they also have other objectives)”.)
rows.ne: • MHPSS गतिविधि भनेको लक्षित जनसमूहको मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याण सुधार गर्न विशेष रूपमा तयार गरिएको गतिविधि हो। मोड्युल 1 मा छलफल गरिएझैँ, कल्याणमा सकारात्मक प्रभाव पार्न सक्ने धेरै कारक छन्; ती सबैलाई MHPSS गतिविधिहरूका रूपमा गणना गरिँदैन। उदाहरणका लागि, खेलकुद खेल्न बालबालिकालाई एक ठाउँमा ल्याउँदा उनीहरूको कल्याणमा सकारात्मक प्रभाव पर्न सक्छ। तर खेलकुद कार्यक्रम विशेष रूपमा बालबालिकाको कल्याण सुधार गर्न तयार गरिएको भए मात्र यसलाई MSP गतिविधि 3.6 अन्तर्गत गणना गरिनेछ (गतिविधि 3.6 को परिचय हेर्नुहोस्: “MSP का प्रयोजनका लागि, ‘बालबालिकाको मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याणका लागि सामूहिक गतिविधि’ भन्नाले मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याण सुधारसँग सम्बन्धित स्पष्ट उद्देश्य भएका र सम्बन्धित सूचकहरू मापन गर्ने गतिविधिहरूलाई जनाउँछ, चाहे तिनका अन्य उद्देश्य पनि होऊन् वा नहोऊन्।”)।
rows.bt: • An MHPSS activity is an activity specifically designed to improve the mental health and psychosocial well-being of the target population. As discussed in Module 1, there are many factors that can have a positive effect on well-being; not all of them are counted as MHPSS activities. For example, bringing children together to play sports may have a positive effect on their well-being. But it will be counted under MSP activity 3.6 only if the sports programme is specifically designed to improve children's well-being (see the introduction to activity 3.6: “For the purposes of the MSP, ‘group activities for children's mental health and psychosocial well-being’ refers to activities that have clear objectives related to improving mental health and psychosocial well-being and measure the related indicators, whether or not they also have other objectives.”).
rows.note: Clinical phrases reuse the supplied unreviewed candidates T157 and T005, also present in the supplied activity 3.6 candidate. Native-language and domain review remain pending; this is not a validated instrument item.

rows.en: • Section 3 activities should be available and accessible to all.
rows.ne: • खण्ड 3 का गतिविधिहरू सबैका लागि उपलब्ध र पहुँचयोग्य हुनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: • The activities in Section 3 should be available and accessible to everyone.

rows.en: • Activities from Section 4 should be implemented as well if relevant to the context, i.e., infectious disease outbreak; working with people deprived of their liberty.
rows.ne: • सन्दर्भसँग सान्दर्भिक भएमा खण्ड 4 का गतिविधिहरू पनि कार्यान्वयन गर्नु पर्छ, अर्थात् सरुवा रोगको प्रकोपको अवस्थामा वा आफ्नो स्वतन्त्रताबाट वञ्चित गरिएका व्यक्तिहरूसँग काम गर्दा।
rows.bt: • If relevant to the context, the activities in Section 4 must also be implemented, that is, in the event of an outbreak of a communicable disease or when working with persons deprived of their liberty.
rows.note: The draft retains the conditional recommendation to implement Section 4 activities as well and preserves both specified contexts. The draft's 'it is appropriate to implement' weakens the source's conditional 'should be implemented'. The repair restores the conditional obligation. “Must also be implemented” strengthens the source’s conditional “should be implemented” from a recommendation to a requirement.

rows.en: • No single organization is expected to implement all programme activities. Rather, organizations must coordinate and work together across sectors/AORs to ensure that activities are implemented and that a comprehensive response is delivered in each geographical area.
rows.ne: • कुनै एउटै संस्थाले सबै कार्यक्रमगत गतिविधिहरू कार्यान्वयन गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छैन। बरु, प्रत्येक भौगोलिक क्षेत्रमा गतिविधिहरू कार्यान्वयन हुने र समग्र प्रतिकार्य प्रदान गरिने सुनिश्चित गर्न संस्थाहरूले क्षेत्रहरू/AORs बीच अनिवार्य रूपमा समन्वय गरी मिलेर काम गर्नुपर्छ।
rows.bt: • No single organization is expected to implement all programmatic activities. Rather, organizations must coordinate across sectors/AORs and work together to ensure that activities are implemented in each geographical area and that an overall response is provided.
rows.note: Recurring coordination acronym AORs has no supplied glossary entry or expansion. It is retained exactly; a glossary proposal requests confirmation rather than inventing an expansion. The BT renders the source obligation must as should. The revision makes the mandatory force explicit. AORs remains unchanged and unexpanded; its technical interpretation remains pending review. The BT replaces a comprehensive response with an overall response and explicitly applies each geographical area to activity implementation rather than to delivery of the response.

rows.en: • These MHPSS activities are not new, they operationalize existing guidance.
rows.ne: • यी MHPSS गतिविधिहरू नयाँ होइनन्; यिनले विद्यमान मार्गदर्शनलाई कार्यरूप दिन्छन्।
rows.bt: • These MHPSS activities are not new; they put existing guidance into practice.

rows.en: Note for facilitators
rows.ne: सहजीकरणकर्ताका लागि टिप्पणी
rows.bt: Note for the facilitator

rows.en: You can divide the activities based on the composition of the participants across sectors/clusters/AORs, assigning the most relevant activities accordingly E.g.
rows.ne: विभिन्न क्षेत्रहरू/क्लस्टर/AORs बाट आएका सहभागीहरूको संरचनाका आधारमा गतिविधिहरू बाँड्न र सोहीअनुसार सबैभन्दा सान्दर्भिक गतिविधिहरू जिम्मा दिन सक्नुहुन्छ। उदाहरणका लागि:
rows.bt: You can distribute activities based on the composition of participants from different sectors/clusters/AORs and assign the most relevant activities accordingly. For example:
rows.note: AORs is retained exactly because no glossary entry or source expansion is supplied.

rows.en: • Activities 3.6 and 3.8 should be assigned to an Education actor and a Child Protection actor working together, if possible,
rows.ne: • सम्भव भएमा, गतिविधि 3.6 र 3.8 शिक्षा क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत एक पक्ष र बाल संरक्षण क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत एक पक्षलाई मिलेर काम गर्ने गरी जिम्मा दिनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: • If possible, activities 3.6 and 3.8 should be assigned to one actor working in the education sector and one actor working in the child protection sector so that they work together.

rows.en: • Activity 3.9 should be assigned to GBV actors, if any are present.
rows.ne: • GBV क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत पक्षहरू उपस्थित भएमा, गतिविधि 3.9 उनीहरूलाई जिम्मा दिनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: • If actors working in the GBV sector are present, activity 3.9 should be assigned to them.

rows.en: • Activity 3.10 should be assigned to Health actors, if any are present.
rows.ne: • स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्रका सम्बद्ध पक्षहरू उपस्थित भएमा, गतिविधि 3.10 उनीहरूलाई जिम्मा दिनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: • If relevant actors from the health sector are present, activity 3.10 should be assigned to them.

rows.en: • Activity 3.11 should be assigned to a Health actor and a GBV actor working together, if possible.
rows.ne: • सम्भव भएमा, गतिविधि 3.11 सँगै काम गर्ने स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्रका एक कर्ता र GBV क्षेत्रका एक कर्तालाई संयुक्त रूपमा जिम्मा दिनुपर्छ।
rows.bt: • If possible, activity 3.11 should be jointly assigned to one actor from the health sector and one actor from the GBV sector working together.
rows.note: Ordinary activity-assignment guidance, not a clinical check or validated instrument item. Preserves joint responsibility and the condition 'if possible'.

rows.en: It may be helpful to take a break or do an energizer between this activity and the next one (‘Matching MHPSS Activities to the MSP’) or to do the following activity on the next day.
rows.ne: यस गतिविधि र अर्को गतिविधि (‘MHPSS गतिविधिहरूलाई MSP सँग मिलाउने’) बीच विश्राम लिनु वा स्फूर्ति जगाउने अभ्यास गर्नु, वा अर्को गतिविधि अर्को दिन गर्नु उपयोगी हुन सक्छ।
rows.bt: It may be useful to take a break or do an energizing exercise between this activity and the next activity (‘Aligning MHPSS activities with the MSP’), or to do the next activity the next day.
rows.note: Preserves the alternatives of a break, an energizer, or conducting the following activity the next day. The original Nepali can refer to the activity after the next activity rather than the immediately following activity. It also changes the final option from potentially helpful to merely possible. The revision identifies the next activity and applies ‘may be helpful’ to all alternatives.

rows.en: Online facilitation
rows.ne: अनलाइन सहजीकरण
rows.bt: Online facilitation
rows.note: The recurring term 'facilitation' is absent from G-0.3; proposed wording is listed separately.

rows.en: Shareable document listing the questions on the slide.
rows.ne: स्लाइडमा भएका प्रश्नहरूको सूची समावेश गरिएको, साझा गर्न मिल्ने कागजात।
rows.bt: A shareable document containing the list of questions on the slide.
rows.note: Preserves the document description rather than adding an instruction to create it. The recurring term 'slide' needs a glossary entry.

rows.en: Ask participants to prepare one to two slides per activity (instead of flip charts) and share their slides with you via email.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूलाई प्रत्येक गतिविधिका लागि (फ्लिप चार्टको सट्टा) एकदेखि दुईवटा स्लाइड तयार गर्न र ती स्लाइड इमेलमार्फत तपाईंसँग साझा गर्न भन्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Ask participants to prepare one to two slides for each activity (instead of a flip chart) and share those slides with you by email.
rows.note: The recurring terms 'participants' and 'slide' are absent from G-0.3. Preserves the per-activity quantity and email recipient.

rows.en: You can also create a shared slide file using Google or another platform and allow participants to work within that file.
rows.ne: तपाईंले Google वा अर्को प्लेटफर्म प्रयोग गरेर साझा स्लाइड फाइल पनि बनाउन र सहभागीहरूलाई त्यही फाइलमा काम गर्न दिन सक्नुहुन्छ।
rows.bt: You can also create a shared slide file using Google or another platform and let participants work in that same file.
rows.note: Uses proposed wording for 'slide' and 'participants'; preserves Google as one platform option.

rows.en: Or you could create slides with the MSP activity numbers and names in advance and distribute the links to these for each group to work in.
rows.ne: वा तपाईंले प्रत्येक MSP गतिविधिको नम्बर र नाम राखेर पहिले नै स्लाइडहरू तयार गर्न र प्रत्येक समूहले तिनमा काम गर्न सक्ने गरी तिनका लिङ्कहरू वितरण गर्न सक्नुहुन्छ।
rows.bt: Or you can prepare slides in advance with the number and name of each MSP activity and distribute their links so that each group can work on them.
rows.note: The recurring term 'slide' lacks a glossary entry. Preserves advance preparation, activity numbers and names, and links for each group.

rows.en: After all groups have shared their slides, compile them (in order) and share the full slide deck with participants via email or in the chat.
rows.ne: सबै समूहले आआफ्ना स्लाइड साझा गरिसकेपछि, तिनलाई क्रम मिलाएर एकत्रित गर्नुहोस् र सम्पूर्ण स्लाइड सङ्ग्रह सहभागीहरूसँग इमेलमार्फत वा च्याटमा साझा गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: After all groups have shared their own slides, put them in order and compile them, and share the entire slide collection with participants by email or in the chat.
rows.note: Uses proposed wording for 'slide' and 'participants'. The complete slide deck, rather than individual selections, must be shared in order.

rows.en: Give them time to go through the slides and encourage them to note questions they may have on specific activities.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूलाई स्लाइडहरू हेर्न समय दिनुहोस् र कुनै खास गतिविधिबारे उनीहरूका प्रश्न भएमा ती टिपोट गर्न प्रोत्साहन दिनुहोस्।
rows.bt: Give participants time to look at the slides and encourage them to note down any questions they have about a particular activity.
rows.note: Uses proposed wording for 'participants' and 'slide'; questions remain tied to specific activities.

rows.en: After participants have had a chance to review the slides, present them on the screen and ask each group to say a few words about their activities, focusing on the purpose of the activity and target groups for each activity.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूले स्लाइडहरू समीक्षा गर्ने अवसर पाएपछि, ती स्लाइड पर्दामा प्रस्तुत गर्नुहोस् र प्रत्येक समूहलाई हरेक गतिविधिको उद्देश्य र लक्षित समूहहरूमा ध्यान केन्द्रित गर्दै आफ्ना गतिविधिबारे छोटकरीमा बोल्न भन्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: After participants have had an opportunity to review the slides, present those slides on the screen and ask each group to speak briefly about their activities, focusing on the purpose and target groups of each activity.
rows.note: Ordinary facilitation guidance, not a validated check. Uses proposed wording for 'participants' and 'slide' and preserves both the purpose and target groups of each activity.

rows.en: Discuss as described for the in-person facilitation.
rows.ne: प्रत्यक्ष उपस्थितिमा गरिने सहजीकरणका लागि वर्णन गरिएअनुसार छलफल गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Conduct the discussion as described for in-person facilitation.
rows.note: Uses the proposed term for 'facilitation'; retains the reference to the in-person instructions without adding their content.

rows.en: Note for facilitators
rows.ne: सहजीकरणकर्ताका लागि टिप्पणी
rows.bt: Note for the facilitator
rows.note: Uses the supplied candidate for 'facilitators'.

rows.en: Use the time it takes for you to compile the slides shared by participants to give participants a short break.
rows.ne: सहभागीहरूले साझा गरेका स्लाइडहरू एकत्रित गर्न तपाईंलाई लाग्ने समयलाई सहभागीहरूलाई छोटो विश्राम दिने अवसरका रूपमा प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: Use the time it takes you to compile the slides shared by participants as an opportunity to give participants a short break.
rows.note: Uses proposed wording for 'participants' and 'slide'; the short break coincides with the time needed to compile their slides.
